_comment: Phase 5 progression. Mining damage: a material yields 1 unit per `hp` damage. Tools deal `power` per swing every `interval` seconds, or `dps` while held (power tools). A tool (or machine) can only work material whose hardness <= its `max_hardness`.

tools.title: Rock Hammer
tools.desc: Grandpa's old hammer. Stone and coal only.

tools.title: Worn Pickaxe
tools.desc: Worn but sound. Bites into stone and can crack iron.

tools.title: Reinforced Pickaxe
tools.desc: Steel-tipped. Every swing takes a real chunk.

tools.title: Corded Rock Drill
tools.desc: Hold to drill. Needs a corded supply. Cuts copper veins.

stages.title: Grandpa's Legacy
stages.goal: Break stone with Grandpa's hammer, clear the overgrown site and sell what you cut.

stages.title: Better Tools
stages.goal: Earn $150, clear the site, get Grandpa's excavator running and haul away the first soil. Then buy better hand tools at the workbench.

stages.title: The Workshop
stages.goal: Earn $600 and own a pickaxe. The workshop sells heavier, more specialised tools.

stages.title: Breaking Ground
stages.goal: Earn $1,800 and make a workbench upgrade. Start processing stone.

stages.title: First Employee
stages.goal: Earn $4,000, find iron and run a crusher. Then you can hire help.

stages.title: Power and Pressure
stages.goal: Earn $9,000, hire a worker and sell crushed stone. Powered tools come next.

stages.title: Moving Mountains
stages.goal: Earn $20,000, own a crusher and open the first bench of the quarry.

stages.title: Industrial Quarry
stages.goal: Earn $45,000 and keep the first bench open. (Further industrial equipment arrives in a later update.)

stages.title: Deeper Ground
stages.goal: Earn $100,000 and open the third level.

stages.title: Beneath the Mountain
stages.goal: Earn $600,000 and reach the lowest level. (Future content.)

hillside_face_01.title: Hillside Face
hillside_face_01._comment: Phase 6.1: first excavatable hillside, cut into the west rim. 6 columns deep (x, back wall at the west) by 12 wide (z). Only the east face is open; the other sides are solid hill, so rock is mined from the front and the cut deepens. Never resize an existing formation: saves store columns by count.

pit_band_01.title: Basin Bench
pit_band_01._comment: Phase 6.3b: a curved bench band inside the starting basin: 16 angular slices x 6 rings x 3 tiers (tops flush with the plateau). Only the inner ring is open; mining it pushes the face outward toward the basin wall. Angles are in the pit frame (0 deg = +x, -90 deg = toward the far wall).

fossil._comment: Phase 7.6: a fossil is buried in the gold bench of the lowest level. It is exposed only when the listed columns have really been mined out. The choice between the two buyers is final.
fossil.found_text:
The last of the stone falls away and there it is: a spine as long as a truck, ribs curving out of the rock like the hull of an old boat, and a skull with teeth the size of your hand. It is not stone. It is a skeleton, and it is enormous.

Nobody has stood here and seen this for millions of years.
toast: The lowest level has uncovered a huge fossil. Go and look (E).

collector.title: Sell to the collector
collector.pitch: A private collector, Mr. Vane, has heard rumours and offers $75,000 for the whole skeleton, crated and gone by the end of the week. It will hang in his private gallery.

scientist.title: Give it to the scientist
scientist.pitch: Dr. Evelyn Marsh of the university can pay only $2,000 towards the cost of the dig. But she will study it, put it on display for everyone, and her name for you will be 'the discoverer'.

fossil.confirm: This cannot be undone. Once you choose, the other buyer is gone for good.

results.collector: Mr. Vane's crew crates the bones and a truck takes them away. $75,000 lands in your account.
results.scientist: Dr. Marsh's team arrives the next morning, delighted. They cry a little. $2,000 and a promise: the university will keep in touch.

walter._comment: Phase 7.5: Walter is alive and retiring, not dead. Intro scene, timed visits and journal. Conditions: stage (id), quarry_level, cleaned (site cleanup done). Visits show once, in the morning/afternoon, when the player talks to him.

lockbox.title: The lockbox
lockbox.text: Under the first rock I cleared there was Walter's old lockbox: a photo of the 1971 crew, notes about copper and gold below the north bench, and a savings bond.

handover.title: The handover
handover.text: Walter handed me the quarry and his old hammer. He is retiring, but he lives down the road and says he will look in on the place.

first_crew.title: A helping hand
first_crew.text: Walter says a quarry is a team sport: a good crew works while you rest. Pay them fairly and they will stay.

machines.title: Machines
machines.text: Walter admits he never owned a proper crusher or loader. 'Muscle gets you started. Machines get you finished.'

first_bench.title: The first bench
first_bench.text: The surface is opening up. Walter remembers the old crew standing on a floor much lower than this, and he says the stone down there looks different.

deep_dig.title: Going deep
deep_dig.text: Walter keeps looking at the lower levels. 'My father said the oldest things lie at the bottom. I never got far enough to see.'

big_dig.title: A real quarry
big_dig.text: Walter walked the rim for a long while. 'It's what I always wanted it to be.'

fossil_found.title: The thing in the rock
fossil_found.text: Something huge lay in the gold bench of the lowest level: a skeleton, ribs and spine and a skull full of teeth. Walter says his father always said so.

fossil_collector.title: Sold to the collector
fossil_collector.text: I sold the skeleton to Mr. Vane for $75,000. It is hanging in a private gallery now, where nobody will see it.

fossil_scientist.title: Given to the scientist
fossil_scientist.text: Dr. Marsh and her team took the skeleton for the university. I got $2,000 and the feeling of having done something right.

companion_egg.title: The egg
companion_egg.text: Dr. Marsh left an egg on the porch. It is warm and it moves a little. It should hatch in a couple of days.

companion_born.title: A new family member
companion_born.text: The egg hatched. I have a dinosaur. Walter says he has never seen anything like it.

companion_adult.title: All grown up
companion_adult.text: My dinosaur is fully grown. It can break rock with its tail.

level1_records.title: Old photographs and records
level1_records.text: Behind a rusty cabinet in the office: photographs of the 1971 crew, and ledgers in Walter's handwriting. The last good year is circled.

level2_geology.title: Geological notes
level2_geology.text: Walter's notes on the first bench: 'Strange banding in the rock below. The layers do not match the survey. Ask Evelyn.'

level3_sketch.title: A strange sketch
level3_sketch.text: A pencil sketch tucked into a notebook: a long spine, curved ribs, a heavy club of a tail. Under it, in Walter's hand: 'Dad was not making it up.'

lines.speaker: DR. EVELYN MARSH
lines.text: Hello again. I promised I would come back.

lines.speaker: DR. EVELYN MARSH
lines.text: We found something odd inside the rock your fossil came from: an egg, still sealed. It should not be viable. It is.

lines.speaker: DR. EVELYN MARSH
lines.text: Keep it warm and dry. It will hatch in a couple of days. Please look after it.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Heard you're thinking about hiring. Good. One pair of hands only goes so far.
Treat them well, learn what they're good at, and let them get on with it. A crew that is respected works twice as hard.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: A crusher and a loader! In my day we had a mule and a bad attitude.
Cut into the hillside from the front and work down, one bench at a time. And keep your crew fed with something to haul - idle machines eat money.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: You opened the first bench. I stood about there, forty years ago, and thought I'd never get any lower.
Go on down the ramp if you like. The coal and iron are better the deeper you go. And rock down there is older than anything in town.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Copper and iron on level three. Now you are cutting where I only ever dreamed.
My father used to say the oldest things in this hill lie right at the bottom. Mind the walls, and take your time.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Look at this. Look at all of it.
I thought I'd be too old to see it. I'm glad I wasn't. This is a real quarry now, kiddo.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
lines.text: I thought I'd never see one of those again.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
lines.text: Let's just say there's a reason I never sold this mountain.

lines.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
lines.text: Whoever you sell it to, kiddo, it's yours to decide. I'll back you either way.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Seventy-five thousand. Well. That is a lot of money for some old bones.
I won't say I'd have done the same. I won't say I wouldn't have. It is your quarry now.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Two thousand dollars and a whole university at your door. I like that.
You did right by it, kiddo. Whatever happens next, that skeleton is where it belongs.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Is that an egg on the porch? Dr. Marsh left it for you?
Well, I never. Keep it warm and dry. I raised chickens once, how hard can it be?

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: It hatched! Look at that little face.
You are going to have to feed it. Or at least be nice to it. It will follow you around the quarry like a puppy.

visits.title: WALTER DROPS BY
lines: Would you look at the size of it. And it can break rock with its tail!
In fifty years of working this quarry I never had a helper like that. Look after it, kiddo.

cinematic.text: Well, look who finally decided to show up.
Don't sound so surprised. I've only been working since dinosaurs were walking around.
Here. The keys. All of them.
Bank wants the place. I told them my grandkid would have it running again in no time.
Relax. You've got my hammer. That's how I started.
There's more in that hill than anyone thinks. Just gotta keep digging.

first_clear.title: GRANDPA'S LOCKBOX
first_clear.text:
Under the last of the rock sits a rusted lockbox. Inside:

- A faded photo of the crew in 1971, standing on this same floor.
- Mining records: 'Core sample, 3.5 m below the north bench: copper staining, trace gold.'
- A note: 'Didn't have the machines to go deeper. Maybe you will.'

There's also an old savings bond. It's still good.

story.intro2:
1. Left click swings your hammer. Cut the weeds and break the rubble heaps. The HUD counts the cleanup.

2. Take the stone to the office and sell it on the computer (SALES).

3. Spend your first money at the workbench in the TOOL SHED: a pickaxe comes first.

4. When it gets dark (after 17:00) walk to the house by the garage and press E on the bed to sleep. Sleeping saves the game and starts a new morning.

5. Clean the whole site and Walt sends money, opens the hillside and the north gate.

cleanup._comment: Phase 6.2 tutorial, moved to Area 1: the weeds and rubble now lie in the starter cut north of the operations yard (never in the yard). Positions are fixed so saves can store what is left; item ids (w0.., h0..) keep their meaning.
cleanup.gift_text:
Kiddo,

I heard you cleaned the old place up. I knew you would.

Now the real rock is open to you: the hillside behind the yard. Cut it from the front, one section at a time, and it will give up good stone.

I'm sending what I had put away. Spend it on a drill when you are ready. Machines are how we cut the big blocks.

- Grandpa Walt

pit_zone._comment: Phase 8.7: a 160 x 156 m plateau (rim at 0) with the 128 x 120 m starting basin (floor -3.6). Four working levels are cut into the basin floor as nested terraced pits (see quarry_levels).

world._comment: Phase 7.1. The industrial hub is the yard inside the cliff ring (x -23.5..23.5, z -6..23.5, plus the east expansion); it is the permanent business area and is never excavated. The main quarry is the pit zone reached through the north-east gate (see pit_zone), where all four levels are cut.

quarry_levels._comment: Four levels of ONE continuous quarry (Phase 7.2). 'formations' are cut in that level; 'unlock' is the share of the PREVIOUS level that must be excavated before the level's rock can be mined (the shell, ramp and walls are always there, under the flush columns). 'pit' (pit frame): rect = [x0, z0, x1, z1] of the whole pit including its ramp strip on the west side; ramp_w = width of that strip; the ramp runs along z from the south end (z1, previous floor) down to the north end (z0, this floor); the columns fill the rest of the rectangle. Phase 8.7: pit = rect [x0,z0,x1,z1] with a haul-road strip of ramp_w on `side` (W/E): the ramp starts at the `ramp_top` end (south/north) and falls ramp_run metres to the level floor, the rest of the strip is flat road. `roads` = rects of this level's own rock that are cut away the moment the level opens, so the haul road is never blocked. Phase 8.7: pit = rect [x0,z0,x1,z1] with a haul-road strip of ramp_w on `side` (W/E): the ramp starts at the `ramp_top` end (south/north) and falls ramp_run metres to the level floor, the rest of the strip is flat road. `roads` = rects of this level's own rock that are cut away the moment the level opens, so the haul road is never blocked.
quarry_levels.title: Surface Operations

companion._comment: Phase 7.7: Dr. Marsh's team leaves the egg (scientist route only). Days are in-game days. Stages: egg -> hatchling -> juvenile -> adult. Tail smash: damage per hit and the hardest rock the companion can break (the same hardness rule as the player's tools).
companion.arrival_text: Dr. Marsh sets the egg in a straw nest by the yard. It is the size of a watermelon and warm to the touch. 'Keep it warm and dry,' she says. 'It should hatch in a couple of days.'
companion.hatch_text: The egg cracks, wobbles, and a small, wet, very serious head pokes out. It looks at you and decides you are its family.
companion.adult_text: %s has grown into a full-size dinosaur. It can smash open hard rock with its tail now.
companion.juvenile_text: %s is growing fast. It is big enough to smash soft rock with its tail now (press T while looking at rock).

walter_mining_lines.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
walter_mining_lines.text: All I needed was a dinosaur.

lines.speaker: DR. EVELYN MARSH
lines.text: Hello again. I promised I would come back.

lines.speaker: DR. EVELYN MARSH
lines.text: We found something odd inside the rock your fossil came from: an egg, still sealed. It should not be viable. It is.

lines.speaker: DR. EVELYN MARSH
lines.text: Keep it warm and dry. It will hatch in a couple of days. Please look after it.

quarry_milestones.title: A quarter of the surface
quarry_milestones.text: A quarter of the surface quarry is cut away.

quarry_milestones.title: Half the surface
quarry_milestones.text: Half of the surface quarry is gone.

quarry_milestones.title: The first bench
quarry_milestones.text: Quarry level 2 is open: coal and iron.

quarry_milestones.title: Bench half cut
quarry_milestones.text: Half of the first bench is excavated.

quarry_milestones.title: The deep quarry
quarry_milestones.text: Quarry level 3 is open: richer iron and copper.

quarry_milestones.title: Deep bench half cut
quarry_milestones.text: Half of the deep quarry is excavated.

quarry_milestones.title: The lower quarry
quarry_milestones.text: Quarry level 4 is open: copper and gold.

quarry_milestones.title: Gold!
quarry_milestones.text: The first gold-bearing rock is out of the ground.

legacy_stage_map_comment: Phase 9.1: an old six-stage save lands on the new stage that unlocks everything it already had (manual, tools, crew->first_employee, industry->power_pressure, large->moving_mountains, deep->deeper_ground). Never lower.
unlocks_comment: Phase 9.1 hybrid unlocks: every entry lists what must be true BEFORE the item can be bought (money is the item's price). stage = a stage id; owns = tools/equipment already owned; discover = minerals found; delivered = minerals sold; milestones = built-in or story milestones; earned; quarry_level; story = story flags.

milestone_titles.soil_hauled: Haul 24 loads of soil to the spoil heap

pointed_chisel.title: Pointed Chisel
pointed_chisel.desc: Fast, light taps. Cuts soft stone and coal far quicker than the hammer, but cannot touch iron.

flat_chisel.title: Flat Chisel
flat_chisel.desc: Wide, clean cuts through stone and coal: the best tool for soft rock until you can afford power.

repaired_pickaxe.title: Repaired Pickaxe
repaired_pickaxe.desc: A properly re-handled pickaxe. Solid on stone, coal and iron.

sledgehammer.title: Sledgehammer
sledgehammer.desc: Heavy and slow. Each blow also hits two neighbouring exposed blocks at half strength.

steel_pickaxe.title: Steel Pickaxe
steel_pickaxe.desc: Steel head, steady swing. Gets into copper-hard rock.

hardened_pickaxe.title: Hardened Pickaxe
hardened_pickaxe.desc: Hardened steel: the best hand pick you can buy.

hand_splitter.title: Hand Rock Splitter
hand_splitter.desc: Wedges and drives a seam: each blow also splits up to three neighbouring exposed blocks at 60%.

powered_hammer.title: Powered Hammer
powered_hammer.desc: A motor-driven hammer: quick heavy blows that also hit two neighbours.

pneumatic_chisel.title: Pneumatic Chisel
pneumatic_chisel.desc: Hold to chisel at speed. Superb on stone and coal. Needs the compressor.

air_compressor.title: Air Compressor
air_compressor.desc: Powers the pneumatic tools: every powered tool you hold works 15% faster.

hand_cart.title: Hand Cart
hand_cart.desc: Wheel your load: the bag holds 20 more.

wheelbarrow.title: Wheelbarrow
wheelbarrow.desc: A proper barrow: the bag holds 40 more.

reinforced_wheelbarrow.title: Reinforced Wheelbarrow
reinforced_wheelbarrow.desc: Steel tray, pneumatic tyre: the bag holds 70 more.

gear_comment: Phase 9.2: extra tools and hauling aids beyond the five-tool ladder (saves keep their tier). class: precision / general / impact / equipment / cart. affinity = damage multiplier per mineral; aoe = neighbouring exposed blocks hit at aoe_frac; powered = gets the compressor bonus; model = the ladder tool whose existing 3D model is shown (no unique models yet).
legacy_formations_comment: Phase 8.7 save migration: the old column layout of each re-laid formation (column count and total units). Saves written with that layout are converted by cleared fraction, never reset.

opening._comment: Phase 10.1: Grandpa's broken mini excavator. Three repairs (battery, hydraulic hose, fuel), each a part lying near the workshop that is carried to the machine and fitted. Grandpa waits near the workshop and helps start it.

battery.title: Battery
battery.hint: The battery is flat and corroded... there is a fresh one on the ground by the fence, west of the old truck.

hose.title: Hydraulic hose
hose.hint: The boom hose split years ago. I kept a spare coiled on the ground, a few steps north-west of the old truck.

fuel.title: Fuel can
fuel.hint: She's bone dry. There is a can of diesel by the fence, north-west of the workshop.

start_lines.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
start_lines.text: Good, that's all of it. Stand clear, I'll turn her over.

running_lines.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
running_lines.text: Well, I'll be damned. She still runs.

running_lines.speaker: GRANDPA WALTER
running_lines.text: She only moves loose soil and gravel. Rock is another matter, but it is a start. She is yours.

soil._comment: Phase 10.2: the loose soil of the working ground. Grid cells of `cell` m from `origin` (x, z); a cell holds layers x units_per_layer soil units, layer_h metres each. hp = damage per unit.

areas.title: AREA 1 - STARTER CUT
areas.note: One shallow cut just beyond the yard gate: weeds and rubble, a soil field, the first rock face. Everything the player removes here stays removed.

areas.title: AREA 2 - UPPER WORKING FACE
areas.note: Through the quarry gate and down the corridor to the basin: the curved basin bench of the same excavation, a wider face of rock to cut and haul back toward the yard.

areas.title: AREA 3 - FIRST TERRACE
areas.note: The first lower working surface, cut into the basin floor and reached by the 20 m ramp once enough of the level above is excavated (coal and iron).

areas.title: AREA 4 - INDUSTRIAL BENCH
areas.note: The third level: a broad bench with room for excavators, loaders and trucks. Cut iron and copper, and load trucks for shipment.

areas.title: AREA 5 - DEEP MINERAL BENCH
areas.note: The fourth level, copper side: deeper, harder rock that needs a stronger machine and a working haul route up the ramps.

areas.title: AREA 6 - FINAL INDUSTRIAL CUT
areas.note: The deepest floor of the same excavation: the gold bench. The last contract needs real excavation, recovery and truck shipments.

cleanup_filled._comment: Blueprint world: the weeds and rubble lie ON the quarry's original soil surface in front of the central gate (Area 1, the tutorial zone); clearing them does not lower the ground.
cleanup_filled.gift_text:
Kiddo,

I heard you cleaned the old place up. I knew you would.

Now the real quarry is open to you: start taking the topsoil off, then the gravel and the limestone under it. Cut it level by level and it will give up good stone.

I'm sending what I had put away. Spend it on a drill when you are ready. Machines are how we cut the big benches.
